references.text: This text describes the event itself where the Lord caused the water in the Sea of Reeds to flow back over the Egyptian army, horses, and chariots, destroying them—the same event that Deuteronomy 11:4 refers back to.

The song of Moses and the Israelites describes how the Lord cast horses and riders into the sea, and Pharaoh's chariots were sunk in the Sea of Reeds—the same destruction mentioned in Deuteronomy 11:4.
Summarizes the event where Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and riders went out into the sea, and the Lord caused the water to flow back over them—the same event referred to.
The psalm praises God who threatened the Sea of Reeds until it became dry, and let the water cover the enemies so that none were left—the same event that Deuteronomy 11:4 reminds us of.
Describes how God shook Pharaoh and his army in the Sea of Reeds—the same destruction of the Egyptian army mentioned.
Joshua reminds the people how the Lord sent darkness between them and the Egyptians, and let the sea come over the Egyptians and cover them—the same historical event.
Nehemiah recalls how God saw the distress of the fathers at the Sea of Reeds and cast their pursuers into the depths like stones in mighty waters.
Hebrews mentions that the Israelites passed through the Red Sea as on dry land, while the Egyptians drowned when they tried to do the same.
